name: Congenital Supravalvular Mitral Ring

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Supravalvular Mitral Ring Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Visualization of a fibrous or membranous ridge above the mitral valve leaflets on echocardiography
Evidence of mitral inflow obstruction with elevated transmitral gradients on Doppler studies
Presence of signs of mitral valve stenosis such as exertional dyspnea and pulmonary congestion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of echocardiographic visualization of supravalvular mitral ring with mitral valve obstruction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings; cardiac catheterization may be used for hemodynamic assessment.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Supravalvular fibrous ridge above mitral valve
Mitral inflow obstruction with elevated transmitral gradient
searchTerms: blocked blood flow through mitral valve
mitral valve narrowing with high pressure

common.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to mitral valve obstruction
Pulmonary congestion secondary to mitral stenosis
searchTerms: fluid buildup in lungs from heart
lung congestion due to mitral valve

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.symptomName: Murmur consistent with mitral valve obstruction
searchTerms: abnormal heart sound due to mitral obstruction

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema from right heart strain
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart strain
leg edema due to right heart overload
coughing up blood from lung pressure
blood in sputum due to lung hypertension
lung bleeding from high blood pressure

rare.symptomName: Cyanosis due to severe mitral obstruction
searchTerms: cyanosis from severe heart valve blockage
blue discoloration due to heart obstruction

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing supravalvular mitral ring and mitral inflow obstruction
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
Chest X-ray showing pulmonary venous congestion
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with congenital heart defect syndromes
other: Cardiac catheterization demonstrating elevated left atrial pressure and transmitral gradient

distinguishingFeatures: Mitral valve leaflet thickening and commissural fusion rather than supravalvular ring
Presence of a membrane dividing the left atrium into two chambers
Different anatomical location from supravalvular mitral ring

redFlags: Severe mitral inflow obstruction causing pulmonary edema
Development of atrial fibrillation with risk of thromboembolism
Progressive heart failure symptoms in infancy or early childhood
references: Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Pediatric Cardiac Surgery. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2013.
Anderson RH, Baker EJ, Macartney FJ, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 3rd ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2002.
